attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1, node2, node3, RHEL10) using RabbitMQ 3.13.7 / Erlang 26.2.5.4 from the upstream packagecloud repos. Created a dedicated CA on node1 and issued per-node server certs plus a client cert. Each node's rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none) and exposes AMQP only on 5671/TLS with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, enforcing that only clients presenting a certificate signed by the cluster CA can connect (verified both a successful mTLS handshake+AMQP publish/consume, and a hard TLS 'certificate_required' rejection for a client without a cert). The management HTTP API (15672) and inter-node/clustering ports (4369, 25672) are firewalled via firewalld rich rules to only accept traffic from the cluster's own /24 subnet, while 5671 is open cluster-wide for AMQP clients. All three nodes joined a single RabbitMQ cluster (rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows 3 running/disk nodes, no partitions). Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured each node's boot_id and health baseline, restarted each node one at a time via `systemctl reboot` while the other two retained quorum, polled until each node's exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id (proving an actual reboot, not just a service restart), and re-verified cluster membership, TLS-only listener state, and a live client-cert-authenticated AMQP publish/consume after each restart.
